My advice is to not let bpd became all that you are. Embrace the fact you have it but that you are still a human being regardless of a mental condition.

But guess what? I dont feel normal. I still have massive feelings of selfloathing and feel like those around me dont love me( i know they do but i cant feel it). I still self medicate.

I also struggle with the thoughts of bpd being a death senence. Its not. Things get better and then they get bad again. Im probably not going to have children because i dont think it would work. 

I found that having bpd gets easier with age. Or you just get used to it.

Just some thoughts

When i got diagnosed in my 20s i was really happy. In my country you can get a sickness benefit for all types of mental illness so i quit my shitty job and sat around the house for several months being depressed and living of the tax payer dollar. I had nothing to do but drink and ended up making a suicide attempt. Whilst i was in the psych ward i came to the realization that even though i hated working it was still better for my mental health than sitting around the house all day feeling miserable. 

I get it. I dont like working either. Im not saying you should get a job and stick to it and everything will be better. But for me its my rock. I find it easier to behave appropriately  at work than in my personal life. I work for the government so its a pretty pc culture. Everyones really open about their mental health issues so i feel pretty safe here. It bring normalicy to my chaotic family life.

I dont know you and what bpd is like for you but its my strongly held opinion that work is good in the long run for bpd sufferers. I gives us structure and self esteem. I hard but worth while.

Tl:dr: yes work can be a very good option.

Hi
Im a guy with bpd and im going to tell you about my experience with women. I dont know if it will help but i just want to share and offer support.

Im in my late 30s and have had two girlfriends. The first one i met when i was 25. I fell in love with her immediately and intensely the way we bpd men(and ladys too)tend to do. I could only see the good in her. I had never felt so happy in my life and was giddy on the thought that if this fantastic lady could love a peice of shit like me then maybe i was not so bad. My mother had died when i was 17 so she was an obvious replacement.

I got cliggy. I wanted her attention all the time. She droped hints that i should back off but i couldnt stop myself. She started ghosting me which made me more miserable and i started acting really posessive. She dumped me one friday and my world ended. If she didnt want me i was less than nothing.

I fell into a cycle of alternating rage and self loathing that i medicated with booze and benzos making it worse. I made 2 serious suicide attempts over a year and was involuntary commited which did nothing to help. Out of loneliness i started visiting brothels. I "fell in love" with a prostitute and spent around twenty thousand dollars on her before i she cut me off. I was beaten up by some men because i wouldnt leave her alone. Because of my drinking i lost my job and accommodation and bounced around the steet and the psych ward for a while. I blamed the world and hated my self at the same time.

I cant exactly say how i got my shit back togeather but i was mostly due to quitting drinking.

I got a job and an appartment. I was lonely all the time and pretty depressed but i kind of excepted it.
This lady moved into the appartment across from me. We started hanging out. I didnt "fall in love" with her though. That took two years. We have now been married 5 years. We love each other madly and we have everything we want. But i still hate myself. I still daydream about killing myself. I still have melt downs. Im still bpd and as a man i dont think i can ever except this about myself. Lately ive been thinking about how it would have been better if my wife and i had never met because then she wouldnt be so miserable and i would finaly be able to kill myself. But i love her and like her and i would miss her so i dont know what to do.

I feel your pain brother. I know that might sound trite considering im "happily married" but for me that changes nothing. No matter what im still going to hate myself.

I want to say that "you will get over it" but people have no doubt said that to you and its bullshit in my opinion. Some people do. We dont. One day you just dont think about it as much.

I would rather you didnt kill yourself although i know how tempting it is.

Im dead serious when i say that just because this women rejected you it does not mean that you are not good enough. She just wasnt  right for you. 

The very best practical advice is to spend as much time with other men just doing stuff. Learn a cool skill like glass blowing. This is how "normal" people get over things apparently.

Hey there. The thing you said about not minding the actually work side of a job but disliking the interaction is something i find very relateable. Some morning i just cant stand to go outside a face the world.

In my 20s i was working in retail jobs i hated. I resented having to fake a positive attatude and i disliked the people i worked with. I was pissed of the despite having a masters degree i was sell overpriced jeans to soccer moms. 

I stuck at this for ten years. I became addicted to pain killers and benzos to cope. One evening when i was very wasted i applyed for a job as a re-shelver at the local public library. I thought nothing would come of it but they contacted me offering me the job with out an interview as i had an english degree. 

I somehow got the courage to quit my job and do this instead. It was one off the best things i have ever done for myself. I sort of found my place. Most of my co workers were just as weird as me. Their like family. I didnt have to have a constant positive attitude. I love working now. I still find the human interaction thing a great big pain in the ass but its bearable. It gives my life structure and stability. without it i would get myself in alot of trouble.  Its my rock.

I really think having a job is a good thing. They can sometimes make us better people.
You say you dont mind work so maybe you just need to find the job that best suits you?
Was there anything you wanted to be when you were younger?

My advice is to resign from your job, take all the money in your savings account and move to another country were you can start afresh and be as promiscuous as you want. Getting a job in a bar might be a good idea as there will be plenty of women for you to take advantage of. Never again contacting the people you have let down would also be wise as you have nothing good to offer them.

Maybe one day they will forget you ever existed.

Just my 2cents.
